title: Best Business Verification API: How to Choose the Right One
summary: The best business verification API pulls primary-source registry data, verifies owners, screens watchlists, and feeds your lending decisions.
body_markdown:
Choosing the best business verification API is one of the first big decisions a lending team makes when it moves small business onboarding online. The market is large. The[SBA small business FAQ](https://advocacy.sba.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/FINAL_FAQsAboutSmallBusiness_2026_012826.pdf) counts about 36.2 million US small businesses, based on 2022 Census data, and 82.3% of them have no employees.


Small businesses are also moving their borrowing online. In the[Fed Small Business Credit Survey](https://www.fedsmallbusiness.org/reports/survey/2026/2026-report-on-employer-firms) , 29% of employer-firm applicants sought online fintech lenders in the 2025 survey, up from 17% in 2020. More online applications mean more businesses to verify quickly and accurately.


This guide explains what a business verification API does, which features matter, and how 2026 rule changes affect ownership checks. It also gives you a four-step framework for comparing KYB (know your business) providers and shows how verification fits into a faster lending workflow.


### What Is a Business Verification API?


The best business verification API pulls primary-source registry data, confirms identifiers and owners, screens watchlists, and returns structured results for your decisioning. In plain terms, it tells you whether a business is real, who owns it, and whether anything about it needs a closer look.


An API (application programming interface) is a connection that lets two software systems exchange data automatically. A business verification API is a type of data verification API. It receives details such as a legal name, address, and tax ID, then returns matched records.


KYB is an industry term rather than a regulatory one. It describes customer due diligence for business customers: confirming the entity exists, verifying identifiers, identifying owners, screening sanctions lists, and monitoring over time. Our guide to the[KYB verification process](https://www.lendflow.com/post/kyb-verification) walks through each stage in more detail.


An identity verification API usually checks people, such as an owner's name, date of birth, and ID document. A business verification API checks the company itself, so many lenders use both together. A full KYB platform adds case management, review queues, and dashboards on top of that data.


Verification confirms facts about a business, but your underwriting rules decide whether it should receive credit. The strongest results come when verification outputs flow directly into those rules and risk scores.


### Key Features Every Business Verification API Should Have


Business verification APIs can look alike on a pricing page, but the data underneath varies widely. These three feature groups separate strong APIs from weak ones.


#### Primary Source Data


Primary source data comes directly from the official record keeper, such as the state Secretary of State office where a business registers. Secondary data comes from aggregators that collect, combine, and resell records, which can leave gaps or delays.


Freshness matters because a business can dissolve, lose good standing, or change officers at any time. A data verification API that pulls live registry records can reflect those changes sooner. Aggregated sources still help fill gaps, and[enriching KYB data](https://www.lendflow.com/post/kyb-data-enrichment) with extra sources gives underwriters fuller context.


#### Business Identifiers and Ownership


Identifiers are the numbers and records that tie an application to a real legal entity. When you pair business checks with an API for KYC verification of owners, look for coverage of these items:


- **EIN/TIN match:** Compares the Employer Identification Number (EIN), a federal tax ID, with the legal business name.
- **Registration status:** Shows whether the entity is active and in good standing in its state of formation.
- **Officers and agents:** Lists the officers and registered agents named in public state filings.
- **DUNS number:** Connects the business to its Dun & Bradstreet record, a commercial credit identifier.
- **Beneficial owners:** Identifies each person who owns 25% or more, plus one person with significant control.


Teams that rely on commercial credit files can run[DUNS number lookups via API](https://www.lendflow.com/post/how-to-automate-duns-number-lookups-through-an-api) instead of searching by hand. According to FinCEN's CDD Rule guidance, beneficial owners include each person owning 25% or more, plus one person with significant control.


#### Screening, Monitoring, and Audit Trails


Screening checks the business and its owners against sanctions lists and watchlists, such as the list kept by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). A good KYC API runs these checks on each person tied to the business as well as on the company name.


Monitoring keeps checking after approval and alerts you when a status, owner, or watchlist result changes. This works hand in hand with[continuous underwriting for lenders](https://www.lendflow.com/post/what-is-continuous-underwriting-a-guide-for-lenders) , where credit decisions update as new data arrives.


Audit trails record what was checked, which source answered, and when. Look for timestamped results returned in JSON, a standard data format that your systems can store and your reviewers can share with auditors.


### Why Business Verification Matters More in 2026


The rules around ownership data changed in 2026, and the change puts more weight on the data lenders collect themselves. The[FinCEN interim final rule](https://www.fincen.gov/beneficial-ownership-information-reporting-rule-fact-sheet) , published in March 2025, exempted US companies from beneficial ownership information (BOI) reporting. FinCEN is the Treasury bureau that fights financial crime.


The[FinCEN final rule on BOI reporting](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0603) permanently removed the requirement for US companies and US persons to report BOI, effective August 14, 2026. Foreign entities registered to do business in the US still report their non-US owners. For most domestic applicants, there is no government BOI filing for lenders to lean on.


Ownership checks still apply where the law requires them. The[FinCEN CDD Rule FAQs](https://www.fincen.gov/resources/statutes-and-regulations/cdd-rule-faqs) explain that covered financial institutions must have procedures to identify and verify the beneficial owners of legal entity customers. Covered institutions include federally regulated banks, federally insured credit unions, broker-dealers, and a few other regulated firms.


Here is what that means in practice:


- **BOI filings:** US-formed companies and their US owners no longer report ownership to FinCEN.
- **CDD duties:** Covered institutions must still identify and verify owners of business customers.
- **Re-verification relief:** Since February 2026, FinCEN's CDD Rule guidance lets covered institutions choose to limit re-checks to first account opening, doubts, or risk-based triggers.
- **Non-bank lenders:** The CDD Rule does not directly cover every fintech, so confirm your bank partner's expectations with your compliance team.


The[FBI 2025 Internet Crime Report](https://www.ic3.gov/AnnualReport/Reports/2025_IC3Report.pdf) shows 24,768 business email compromise complaints and $3,046,598,558 in reported losses in 2025. Business email compromise (BEC) is a scam where criminals pose as trusted contacts to redirect payments, a different threat than fake-business onboarding fraud.


BEC still shows how often criminals target business finances. That is a good reason to confirm who you fund and to keep your fraud controls layered across the full lending lifecycle.


Global platforms have one more date to track. The[EU AML Regulation text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX%3A32024R1624) states that the regulation applies from 10 July 2027 and sets a 25% ownership threshold. US-only lenders can treat this as a note, while platforms with EU customers should confirm their KYB providers cover European registries.


### How to Choose the Best Business Verification API


A clear framework helps your team find the best business verification API for its needs using evidence instead of marketing claims. The four steps below build on each other, so start with your use case before you look at pricing.


#### Step 1: Map Your Use Case


Different lending products need different checks, and the right API depends on what you fund. Start by matching your products to the checks they need most:


- **Term loans and lines of credit:** Need full entity, owner, and credit file checks because exposure lasts months or years.
- **Merchant cash advances:** Need fast results, since these advances against future sales often compete on speed.
- **Embedded finance platforms:** Need checks that run inside a partner's product without adding steps for the borrower.
- **Marketplaces and payments:** Need high-volume onboarding plus ongoing monitoring of sellers and merchants.


Next, write down which data fields your underwriting rules actually use, since the best business verification API for you is the one that returns them. That list becomes your scorecard for every vendor demo you schedule.


#### Step 2: Compare Coverage and Data Sources


Coverage claims are hard to compare because providers count states, countries, and data sources in different ways. Ask each KYB provider which states it pulls live, which come from stored copies, and how often stored data refreshes.


Provider Type Main Strength Watch-Out Best Fit


Primary-source US registry API Live Secretary of State pulls with detailed US entity data Limited international coverage US SMB lenders that need fresh status data


Global aggregator Broad country coverage through one contract Data may be secondary and refresh less often Platforms onboarding businesses in many countries


Identity platform Strong person-level KYC and ID document checks Business registry depth may be thinner Teams focused on verifying owners and signers


Orchestration layer Connects several providers and routes requests through waterfalls Results depend on the partners connected Lenders that want flexibility without many separate integrations


A waterfall is a rule that sends a request to a second source when the first one returns no match. If you verify owners too, make sure your identity verification API and business API results can join on the same applicant record.


#### Step 3: Understand Pricing Models


Pricing pages are often vague, so ask for a written quote based on your expected monthly volume. The best KYC API on paper can cost more than planned once you add monitoring, repeat checks, and failed lookups.


Pricing Model How It Works Good For Question to Ask


Per-verification You pay a fee for each lookup Low or uneven volume Are no-match and repeat lookups charged?


Subscription You pay a fixed fee for a volume tier Steady, predictable volume What happens when you exceed the tier?


Enterprise custom You negotiate a contract with volume discounts High volume or many products Which add-ons, such as monitoring, cost extra?


Free tier or trial You get limited lookups at no cost Sandbox testing and proofs of concept Does test data match live production sources?


A free KYC API tier is useful for early testing, but it rarely reflects production volume or support levels.


#### Step 4: Test Before You Commit


A sandbox demo rarely shows how an API handles messy, real applications. Run a sample of recent applications through two or three options in parallel, using the same inputs for each, and track these results:


- **Match rate:** The share of applications that return a confident match on the first request.
- **Manual review rate:** The share flagged for a person to check, which drives your staffing costs.
- **Latency:** The time from request to response, which matters most for instant-decision products.
- **Data gaps:** The states, entity types, or sole proprietors that return thin or empty results.
- **Support quality:** The speed and clarity of vendor answers to your technical and data questions.


Measure the KYC API integration effort during the same test. Note how long your engineers need to map fields, handle errors, and send results into your decision engine.


### Best Practices for Business Verification in Lending


Lendflow's pre-qualified offers drive an average of 42% faster speed to funding. Embedded finance customers operate with 80% smaller teams while converting similar funding volumes. Those results come from connecting data, decisions, and workflows, and verification is one of the first links in that chain.


- **Choose specialized or all-in-one on purpose:** Specialized APIs may go deeper on one check, while all-in-one tools simplify contracts and support.
- **Use orchestration and waterfalls:** Send each request to your preferred source first and fall back automatically when a match fails.
- **Feed results into scoring:** Pass verification fields straight into risk models so they shape the decision instead of sitting in a file.
- **Avoid EIN-only checks:** A matching tax ID does not prove who controls the business or whether it is in good standing.
- **Re-verify on triggers:** Recheck businesses at renewals, new draws, and ownership changes as well as at onboarding.

### Conclusion


The best business verification API gives you fresh, primary-source data, clear ownership results, and screening you can audit. With BOI reporting ended for US companies, the ownership data you collect matters more than it did a year ago.


Start with your use case, compare coverage and pricing models side by side, and test with real applications before you sign. Most importantly, treat verification as one layer in an orchestrated lending workflow, where results feed explainable scoring and faster funding decisions.


### Frequently Asked Questions


These answers cover the questions lending and compliance teams ask most when they compare business verification options.


#### What Is the Difference Between a Business Verification API and a KYB Platform?


A business verification API returns data checks, such as registry status and owner records, directly to your systems. A KYB platform adds review queues, case management, and dashboards on top of that data.


#### Is Verifying an EIN Alone Enough for KYB?


No, because a matching EIN only confirms that a tax ID belongs to a business name. Full KYB also checks registration status, beneficial owners, and watchlist results.


#### Do Lenders Still Need to Identify Beneficial Owners After the 2026 FinCEN Changes?


Covered financial institutions, such as banks and federally insured credit unions, must still identify and verify beneficial owners under the CDD Rule. Non-bank lenders should confirm their obligations and bank partner requirements with their compliance team.


#### How Often Should Businesses Be Re-Verified?


Re-verify at key events such as renewals, new draws, and ownership changes, and use ongoing monitoring to catch status or watchlist changes between those events.


#### Should I Integrate Directly or Through an Orchestration Platform?


A direct integration works well if one provider covers all your needs. An orchestration platform lets you combine several providers, add waterfalls, and swap sources without rebuilding your workflow.
